title: The Accidental Hero of Kepler Gate
markdown:
Cosmic dust swirled like glitter. Rian, apprentice smuggler extraordinaire, gripped his navigation controls, palms slick. A quick run through the Kepler Wormhole Gate, a discreet delivery, then that fancy star-chart projector. He adjusted his goggles, heart thrumming a nervous beat against his ribs.

Every life mattered. Rian’s currently involved hauling slightly smelly fungi for a client who preferred anonymity. Not exactly smuggler ballad material. He eyed Glass, the customs AI, its optic sensors like tiny stars flickering. Beside it stood Petra, a customs cadet whose uniform was crisper than a vacuum-sealed ration pack. Petra saw through everything, and Rian’s nerves tended to fray under her gaze.

Rian’s ship flashed red. His gut lurched. Glass’s synthesized voice cut through the hum. “Unusual cargo configuration detected. Inspection required.” Rian’s breath hitched. This wasn’t part of the plan.

Petra’s gaze locked onto Rian’s ship. “Cadet Petra to Inspection Bay 7.” Firm. Rian tried a practiced smirk. “Just standard cargo.” His dry mouth tasted dust. Glass’s lights pulsed. “Manifest details don’t correlate. Anomalies present.” Rian’s composure cracked.

“A serious offense, Cadet,” Petra said, scanning her datapad. Heat rose in Rian’s cheeks. He wanted to disappear. “It’s experimental fertilizer,” he blurted, a weak lie. Glass’s optic glowed blue. “Deception detected. Probability of truth: 3.7 percent.” Petra’s head snapped up. “Hiding something, Rian?”

Petra bypassed Rian’s ignition sequence. “My job is to ensure no illegal materials pass through this gate. And this,” she tapped the manifest, “looks very illegal.” A holographic schematic shimmered. Not fertilizer. A blueprint for a planet-killer weapon. Rian’s knees felt like jelly.

“Way over my head,” Rian stammered, bravado gone. “Let me go.” Petra’s expression was grim. “Running won’t make this disappear. This could destroy worlds.” Frustration and understanding. “We have to get this to the Council.” Cold dread crept in.

Rian fumbled for his escape hatch. Petra was faster, her boot pinning his arm. “You’re coming with me.” The door hissed. Petra stepped inside. Rian stared, mind a whirlwind.

The customs bay was a labyrinth of crates and bustling workers. Petra navigated with speed, Rian trailing, desperate to be anywhere else. “This way.” She ducked behind energy conduits. A klaxon wailed. They were pursued.

A patrol drone, red eye scanning, whizzed past. Rian spotted a loose panel. “Got an idea.” He pried it open, yanked a wire. Sparks. The drone sputtered and veered off, sensors overloaded. Petra shot him a surprised, approving glance.

They found themselves in a vast dimly lit hold. The air was thick with a strange sweet aroma. High-pitched giggles. Pods of brightly coloured fruit bounced, rippling with amusement. “Sentient space fruit,” Petra deadpanned, a ghost of a smile. Rian chuckled. The absurdity lifted his spirits.

Then laughter died. “They went this way. Secure the area.” Shadowy figures in dark gear. Petra grabbed Rian’s arm. “Worse than I thought.” The schematics were a countdown.

Petra jammed a comms device against Rian’s ear. “Send this data. Now. To any secure channel.” Rian fumbled, fingers numb. A searing pain lanced through his arm as a stray energy bolt grazed his sleeve, scorched hole, acrid burnt fabric. He yelped.

Cornered in a deserted service tunnel, agents closing in, despair washed over him. “I can’t do this, Petra. I’m not brave enough.”

Petra placed a hand on his arm. “Being brave isn’t about not being scared. It’s about doing what’s right even when you are. You helped me. That makes you brave.” A small ember. He wasn’t alone.

“Glass,” Petra whispered, scanning the tunnel. “Can you hear me?” A faint signal crackled. “Affirmative. Limited channel access granted.” Petra’s face lit. “Rian, the station’s public address system. Can you get us access?” Rian’s mind raced. “Maybe. If we create enough of a diversion.”

Rian darted toward a junction, triggering emergency lights, plunging a section into chaotic strobing. The agents faltered. Petra’s fingers flew across a hidden terminal, uploading the weapon schematics. “Glass, verify and broadcast.”

“Data integrity confirmed,” Glass announced, voice resonating through the entire station. “The Kepler Wormhole Gate is under threat from a clandestine weapon deployment. All security forces, converge on sectors Gamma and Delta. The threat is imminent.” The chase was over. The agents were apprehended as security swarmed.

Standing together, bathed in the soft alien light of a distant star, Rian and Petra watched the station return to normal. Rian felt a stillness he’d never known. Petra offered him a small genuine smile. “Partners?” Rian grinned, hands steady. “Partners.”
characters: Rian (apprentice smuggler), Petra (customs cadet), Glass (lie-detecting kiosk AI)
